sections.h2: What does the Madison County Recorder do?
sections.html:
The Madison County Recorder records, indexes and keeps every document that transfers land in the county. The land record begins in 1812, the year the county was created, and it establishes who owns what. Besides deeds, mortgages, liens, trusts and easements, the office records military discharge papers (DD-214) and out-of-county birth certificates and marriage licenses.

The office is at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025, the same building that houses the Treasurer and the Board of Review. The counter opens at half past eight on weekdays and closes at half past four, with holiday closures. The phone is 618-296-4475 and the email is recorder@madisoncountyil.gov.

For a seller, the Recorder is where the sale becomes public record. Recording here puts the sale on the public record. Your title company or closing attorney normally handles the filing, but you should know what the office will look for.

sections.h2: What does a Madison County deed need before it is recorded?
sections.html:
A deed has to meet several state and county requirements, and the Recorder's office will not accept one that misses them. The office's documents page lists these:

  • A completed Illinois Department of Revenue Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a Statement of Exemption.
  • The name and address of the grantee for tax billing purposes, required by 55 ILCS 5/3-5020. Madison County counts as a county of the second class, with a population over 25,000 and not over 1,000,000.
  • A Plat Act Affidavit with every deed, with the form and instructions posted on the county website.
  • A permanent parcel number. A county board resolution requires one on all deeds and documents that transfer property.
  • The name and address of the person to whom the document should be returned.
  • The name and address of whoever prepared the instrument, printed or stamped on its face (55 ILCS 5/3-5022). Court orders, wills, death certificates and instruments signed outside Illinois are excluded.

A release must also give the recorder's document number of the mortgage it releases, or the book and page where applicable. A document number is preferred. If the deed carries money, the office wants the recording fee and the transfer tax paid separately when you pay by check.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies in Madison County?
sections.html:
Two layers of tax apply to the declared price, and both are stated per $500 or part of $500 of taxable consideration. The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500, and the County of Madison collects $.25 per $500. The county's page lists the full set of exemptions in the office, on the website and in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

State of Illinois$.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration
County of Madison$.25 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration

The PTAX declaration asks you to work out the net taxable consideration. The Department of Revenue supplies the forms, and the Recorder cannot take a deed and declaration until all required information is filled in. For questions on the form, call the Recorder, or reach the state revenue agency's Springfield line at 217-782-4568.

Recording fees are set separately. Ask the Recorder's office for the current fee schedule before you mail or send a payment, because the amount depends on the document type.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Madison County Recorder accept?
sections.html:
The office records a long list of instruments, and deeds, mortgages and releases make up most of the volume. The types named on its list include warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, trustee's, executor's, administrator's, guardian's, conservator's, sheriff's and tax deeds, deeds in trust, easements, leases, contracts for deed, mortgage assignments and modifications, mechanic's liens, lis pendens, state and federal tax liens, plats and plats of survey, UCC filings and notices of probate.

A few categories carry their own rules:

  • Plats require the original plat and two copies, one mylar and one paper, plus a surveyor's certificate, a legal description, a school district statement and a 9-1-1 coordinator's certificate.
  • State tax liens trace to Chapter 35 ILCS, Act 5, Article 11, and federal tax liens come through the Internal Revenue Service.
  • A memorandum of judgment must show the court, date, amount, case number, the winning party and the last known address of the losing party.
  • Contracts for deed and sales contracts follow 765 ILCS 86/10-5.

Mortgage releases follow 765 ILCS 905/2. For a seller with an old mortgage, confirm that the lender's release was recorded, because an unrecorded release can stall a closing.

sections.h2: How do you get copies from the Madison County Recorder?
sections.html:
Send copy requests to recordercopies@madisoncountyil.gov with the reference number of the document. The office does not do title searches, so the reference number is what lets staff locate it. Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, and turnaround is 5 to 7 business days, though staff try to move faster.

To find a number yourself, use the parcel number on your tax bill. The county's parcel format breaks down by township, land or lot, map, block and parcel. In the sample 14-2-15-10-20-303-007.001, the first 14 is the old township number, the 2 means a subdivided lot, and the 007 is the parcel with an 001 split suffix. Ending codes show the class: R00 for residential or farm, C00 commercial, A00 agricultural lease and D00 for TIF and enterprise zone parcels.

sections.h2: What does a Madison County seller do about taxes at the Recorder's office?
sections.html:
Most of the tax work happens before the deed reaches the Recorder. Confirm the installments are paid with the Treasurer, which bills in July, September, October and December, so a closing in between can leave a partly paid year. Make sure the grantee's tax bill address is on the deed. The Recorder will not record a deed without it, and a wrong address sends the next bill to the wrong place.

The county has a land record going back more than two centuries, and the title search behind your sale draws on it. If you are selling a house with problems, such as an unreleased old mortgage or a probate gap, have the title company check the Recorder's index early so those items are fixed before the closing date.

sections.h2: How does a Madison County deed fit into a house sale?
sections.html:
A typical sale in Madison County moves in a set order. The title company orders a search against the Recorder's index, the seller signs a deed, the parties complete the PTAX declaration or claim an exemption, and the closer submits everything for recording. The transfer tax is computed from the declared consideration, and the state and county shares are collected together when the deed is accepted.

Because the office will not take a deed missing its required items, errors cost days. The most common fixes come from the list above: a missing parcel number, no return address, no preparer statement, or a Plat Act Affidavit left out of the package. A seller who hands the closer a tax bill with the full parcel number and the buyer's mailing address avoids most of these.

If your property sits inside a subdivision, ask whether a plat covers it, since plats have their own recording rules and may be needed to answer title questions. If you hold the property in a trust, say so at the start, because deeds in trust and trustee's deeds are separate document types on the Recorder's list. Sellers who inherited a home should bring the probate paperwork, since a notice of probate and an executor's or administrator's deed are also recorded documents in this office.

faqs.q: Where is the Madison County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: It is at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025. Weekday hours run from half past eight in the morning to half past four in the afternoon, with holiday closures.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Madison County?
faqs.a: The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration, and Madison County collects $.25 per $500 or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or exemption statement goes with the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a parcel number on my deed?
faqs.a: Yes. A county board resolution requires a permanent parcel number on all deeds and documents affecting transfers of property. Use the number printed on your tax bill.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded document cost?
faqs.a: Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a 5 to 7 business day turnaround. Include the reference number, since the office does not do title searches.

faqs.q: Does the deed need the buyer's address?
faqs.a: Yes. Illinois law requires the grantee's name and address for tax billing purposes on any conveyance recorded in a county of the first or second class, and Madison County is a second class county.
